subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw accept backup exclude patterns in core now, and if so should the permanent contract include auto-loaded `.backupignore`, single-root warnings, and the new JSON/manifest `excludedStats` surface?
rationale: The feature is useful and tied to a canonical open request, but it changes a restore-critical CLI/API surface and sensitive backup scope; automation cannot choose the product/security contract for defaults, opt-in behavior, and external-asset semantics.

options.title: Require a narrowed, rebased exclude design
options.body: Keep the feature path open but require a rebased PR that fixes the source blockers and supplies real backup/verify proof before maintainer review.

options.title: Defer to the canonical issue
options.body: Pause this PR and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/40786 to settle the backup exclude API and security model before implementation resumes.

options.title: Reject core excludes for now
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers decide current backup hardening plus existing `--no-include-workspace`/`--only-config` is the supported near-term surface.

recommendation.title: Require a narrowed, rebased exclude design
recommendation.body: Keep the feature path open but require a rebased PR that fixes the source blockers and supplies real backup/verify proof before maintainer review.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup hardening work makes this the strongest available owner signal for the upgrade and restore-critical backup path.
